blocks.html: Incredible certainly is the ruse and wiliness of Satan, who, like a roaring lion, ever walks about around men, to catch and deceive some one of them, a transfiguring himself oftentimes into an Angel of light, the better to envelop and entice him b; nay, he so well embellishes and adorns his darkness with his colours that to many the very night and obscurity seem to be a splendour and perfect light — as in this unbewitching, in which, under the pretext of piety and of ecclesiastical ceremonies, he grafted a horrible and cruel poison, persuading these poor married people that there was no other means to unbewitch than the superstition of eating hosts and fouaces, thus leaving aside contrition of heart, humiliation of spirit, alms, fasts and prayers, which are the true and excellent exorcisms to present to God c, placing in Him all one's hope, and not in vain superstitions and other such useless things. d

notes.original: A la premiere des S. Pierre. c. v.
notes.gloss: Adversarius vester diabolus tamquam leo rugiens circuit, quaerens quem devoret — your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.

notes.original: A la ſecon de des Corin tans. c. xi.
notes.gloss: Ipse enim Satanas transfigurat se in angelum lucis — Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light. The print's Corintans is as printed.
